correctness.rationale: Gessel gives the needed exact ternary nondivisibility condition. Every modular sum is uniquely represented by ternary digits with two carries and input weights. Direct symbolic closure produces exactly 18 states and an exact integer identity T^2(T-3I)(T-I)^5=0; equality of the first eight histogram values proves the closed forms for every r by an order-eight recurrence. The support converse constructs the digit-sum-zero and one cases explicitly and partitions larger target digit units. The energy equals the weighted second moment of the proven histogram. Two standard-library scripts recalculate the state closure/matrix identity and independent four-input carry energies; direct sums checked through depth ten. No numerical bound or sampled horizon is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The naturally defined nondivisibility-index set of a classical graph enumeration sequence is sparse, with cardinality r(r+3)/2. Its precise sumset, unexpectedly bounded cyclic representation multiplicities, entire histogram, and quartic additive energy address motivated all-depth arithmetic structure. The result supplies a meaningful complete classification rather than an isolated arbitrary modulus example or a restatement of the graph-count congruence. The finite carry-state proof exposes structurally why no fiber exceeds six.
